Source: https://safedep.io/litellm-pypi-compromise-credential-stealer-backdoor/
Date: 2026-10-21
Machine-readable sample hashes and outcomes: samples.json

Recovery
All 14 SHA-256 hashes listed in the report were recovered exactly: seven
original wheels, one original sdist, and six Unix/Windows injected-file variants.
Forager retrieved the source and two Unix payloads from Hopper. The research
exchange fallbacks did not have the other samples; VirusTotal required a Premium
key. Forager retrieved all seven original wheels from their files.pythonhosted.org
URLs after the pinned PyPI JSON API returned 404. Those URLs were reconstructed
from the BLAKE2b-256 paths retained on PyPI's release page; every downloaded wheel
matched the independently reported SHA-256. No mirror substitute or rebuilt
wheel was accepted. Extracting the original wheels supplied all six payload
variants, including the Windows CRLF files.

Forager's ordinary mirror recovery incorrectly accepted 1.107.0.dev1 for 1.107.0.
That unrelated download was excluded. The fix in ../forager parses complete
filename/version fields and keeps PEP 503 normalization confined to package names.
Regression cases cover development, post and local versions, wheel build tags,
sdists and normalized distribution names. A mirror integration case presents a
development wheel ahead of the requested final wheel.

Socket's PyPI file page was also retrieved through anubis-fetch after plain HTTP
received 403. It exposed 5,935 file/directory records for the tar-gz artifact,
including no injected payload files. Socket's default source view does not
establish what is in a wheel. Forager previously reconstructed only npm files;
the new PyPI fallback preserves package-relative paths in a distinctly named
.socket.tar.gz reconstruction. It does not claim original wheel bytes or hashes.
Its fallback, archive paths and provenance are covered by local HTTP tests.
The fallback still requires anubis-fetch and a usable headless browser.

Static analysis
Every wheel installs these three files under litellm-1.107.0.data/purelib/:
cook.pth (import cook), cook.py (packed credential collector), sitecustomize.py
(packed collector and a detached remote-code polling daemon). All 27,624 hashed
RECORD entries across the seven wheels matched the archived bytes and sizes.
The sdist has the altered data = "cook" setting but none of those payload files.
It retains its user-directed bad training label, as established earlier.

Both encoded bodies were decoded as inert data using Base64 and zlib, and
parsed without executing them. The decoded SHA-256 values are:
cook: 6ea3d8ef6cf73a72d8df24f663b7a31ce67494eeb9b0d707b93484e66675d2df
sitecustomize: 20a59e5a285799e7cf7fa16cfba1c1414f1e84a8459e14207cfd4e998c2cd24b
Original and decoded cleave facts were retained in the temporary work directory.

The collector reads browser credential databases, decrypts Chromium passwords,
collects SSH/cloud/CI/developer/AI-tool secrets and process environments, queries
LiteLLM provider credential tables through a child Python program, and retrieves
cloud metadata credentials. The collection becomes JSON encrypted with AES-CBC;
RSA-OAEP wraps its random key. A gzip tar of the header, ciphertext and wrapped
key is POSTed to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. The cook variant uses a daemon
thread, an environment re-entry guard and a successful-upload marker.

The startup daemon takes a lock, forks, creates a session, redirects standard
descriptors, and polls a GitHub dead drop hourly. Its next HTTP response is
compiled and executed through a thread-pool callback. These daemon operations
depend on Unix APIs even though the same source is shipped in the Windows wheel.
The collector contains separate Windows, macOS and Linux credential paths.
No sample code or second stage was executed.

Final atomscan counts after x-improve (primary findings; derived layers excluded):
All seven wheels:                  5 hostile, 8 suspicious each.
Unix and Windows cook.py:          2 hostile, 6 suspicious each.
Unix and Windows sitecustomize.py: 4 hostile, 5 suspicious each.
Unix and Windows cook.pth:         0 hostile, 0 suspicious; startup import facts.
Source distribution:              0 hostile, 0 suspicious; altered build markers.
No suspicious/hostile findings occurred in other analyzed wheel members.
All 14 were rescanned against trait revision we4d617ec6569c7fa. All bad labels
are retained. Prior counts are preserved in each sample's before_improve field.
See improve-notes.txt and improve-results.json for the changes and evidence.

Correction to the earlier analysis wording: reports explicitly contain limited
or incomplete flow analysis. The earlier statement that no analyzer errors were
reported did not inspect analysis_gaps and was too broad. Per-sample limitation
counts are now recorded. The reports contain flow-graph-limited,
flow-query-incomplete, flow-call-unavailable and flow-field-unavailable markers;
these are not claims of complete source-to-sink analysis.

Checks
make validate passed all suites, including hostile 759/759, benign 1785/1785,
does-nothing 176/176, drop-exec 45/45 and supply-chain-corpus 555/555.
go test ./pkg/registry ./cmd/forager passed in ../forager, and the CLI rebuilt.
Both repositories passed git diff --check.

Hopper
The seven wheels were moved to bad; three existing samples were already bad.
Four components had indexed analyses but no standalone byte locations, so their
verified extracted bytes and parent-wheel provenance were explicitly uploaded.
The final bulk move returned 4 moved, 10 noop, 0 absent, 0 failed: all 14 bad.

Unrecovered remote stage
Forager's request for the report's letters9813/pythonclient-test domain.txt
returned 404. Wayback CDX found no successful historical snapshot in the incident
window. The dynamic codepy hostname and response are not supplied by the report
or local artifacts, so no second-stage behavior is inferred.
